thread:
owen: quick update: we shipped the 'latency-first coalescer' canary in us-west-2 at 09:03 PT. it prioritizes assembling microbatches to hit latency SLOs for small-window requests while still batching larger ones for cost.

tara: nice! top-line numbers?

owen: canary window 09:03-09:33 (6% traffic): total requests 10.2k; p50 24ms -> 12ms (-50%); p95 280ms -> 165ms (-41%); p99 640ms -> 480ms (-25%). token-cost per 1k tokens ~-15% due to smarter packing. errors unchanged.

felix: impressive. what workloads were included in the eval? any regressions on rerankers or multi-turn chat?

owen: we ran a stratified eval: short-utterance widgets, mid-length chat, and re-ranker traces (~4k samples). re-rankers unchanged (they prefer larger batches so coalescer defers), multi-turn kept their KV path untouched. only narrow regressions on a few synthetic oracle prompts where aggressive coalescing added a 1-token delay; we added a tiny micro-priority preemption to avoid delaying responses expected under 30ms.

deploy-bot: rollout: coalescer-service v4.0.0 -> canary(6%) (deploy id: d-20260320-08)

sasha: are there new synthetic checks or alerts? last time a batching change caused midnight p99 spikes.

owen: yes: synthetic suite added for high-concurrency short requests every 1m and a KV-warmup monitor. alerting rules: coalescer/us-west-2 p95 > baseline*1.5 -> @eng-oncall; p99 > baseline*1.6 -> paged. auto-rollback: p95 > baseline*1.8 for 3m OR error-rate > baseline*2 for 5m.

product-bot: note added for weekly product update: expected cost impact - ~15% for small-request-heavy routes; recommend adding a console tile for 'coalescer adoption' and savings estimate.

mike: Dedicated customers question: does model placement change on reserved pools?

owen: no change to Dedicated placement or billing. coalescer only affects request scheduling inside the shared runtime. billing team notified to prep a FAQ.

felix: what's ramp plan?

owen: ramp 6% -> 25% in 12h if p95 within 1.6x baseline -> 70% in 36h -> 100% in 72h. continuous A/B evals will run and we'll open a short dogfood window for product teams to try targeted routes.

sre-bot: synthetic monitors scheduled and dashboard tile created: route "latency-first-coalescer" shows p50/p95/p99 and adoption.

sasha: action items: 1) finish extended evals on edge synthetic oracles (felix) 2) add console savings tile and blurb (owen/product) 3) watch canary and synthetic alerts (sre) 4) billing FAQ (mike).

tara: great win, thanks everyone. please escalate immediately if we see any unexpected tail spikes. :rocket:
